latest.content:

Revolution Beauty Group PLC

REVOLUTION BEAUTY GROUP PLC
("Revolution Beauty", the "Group" or the "Company")
HALF YEAR TRADING UPDATE
Notice of results to end August 2026
Investor presentation
Revolution Beauty Group plc (AIM: REVB), the multi-channel mass beauty brand, is very pleased to announce a successful first half of FY27 as its turnaround strategy gathers pace.
The Group expects to report adjusted EBITDA of not less than £2m which compares to a £12.5m loss in the first half of the previous year. Despite the first half of the prior year having been materially flattered at the top line by discount sales to generate cash and sales of discontinued brands and SKUs, this year’s first half produced revenues broadly in line with last year but with a gross margin more than 10 percentage points higher. We also continued with the strong cost discipline that has enabled the business to demonstrate profitability at the EBITDA level in every month for the last twelve months.
Looking forward, the second half of the year seasonally contributes more than the first half. The Company’s order books suggest that the changes management have made to products and ranges are beginning to have a positive impact with our retail customers. The Group’s online sales, which are a good forward indicator, grew 22% in the first half of the year as against the comparable period last year. The Company will provide greater detail in its interim results in October but at this stage the Board considers that the Group is trading comfortably ahead of market expectations.
Half Year Results and Investor Presentation
Revolution Beauty will announce its interim results for the six months ended 31 August 2026 on Tuesday 27 October 2026.
The Company will host a presentation for all existing and potential shareholders on the Investor Meet Company platform on 27 October 2026 at 11:00 am BST. The presentation will be hosted by Tom Allsworth, CEO and Neil Catto, CFO. Questions can be submitted pre-event via the Investor Meet Company dashboard up until 26 October 2026 at 9:00 am BST, or at any time during the presentation. Investors can sign up to Investor Meet Company for free and add to meet Revolution Beauty via:
https://www.investormeetcompany.com/revolution-beauty-group-plc/register-investor
Investors who already follow Revolution Beauty on the Investor Meet Company platform will automatically be invited.
The information contained within this announcement is deemed to constitute inside information as stipulated under the retained EU law version of the Market Abuse Regulation (EU) No. 596/2014 (the "UK MAR") which is part of UK law by virtue of the European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018. The information is disclosed in accordance with the Company's obligations under Article 17 of the UK MAR. Upon the publication of this announcement, this inside information is now considered to be in the public domain.

About Revolution Beauty
Revolution Beauty is a global mass beauty business which operates a multi brand, multi category strategy and sells its products both direct-to-consumer (DTC) via its e-commerce operations, and in physical and digital retailers through wholesale relationships.
Today, the Group has a retail footprint of c.17,500 doors across leading retail chains in the UK, USA and other international markets. Revolution Beauty has access to a wide customer base, predominantly aged between 16 and 35, through its digital partners and own DTC platform. It has established and invested to streamline its supply chain with its own manufacturing facility in the UK, and third-party warehousing facilities across the UK and in the USA. The Group has offices in the UK and the USA. Revolution Beauty currently employs 231 people.

company_30s.what_they_do: Revolution Beauty is a cosmetics retailer that sells a wide range of makeup, skincare, and haircare products through its own stores, e‑commerce site and wholesale channels. It focuses on trendy, affordable brands and frequently launches limited‑edition collections to drive repeat traffic.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The beauty sector is a multi‑billion‑pound market that continues to grow as consumers seek high‑quality yet inexpensive products. Revolution Beauty’s strategy of fast‑turnover, low‑price items and strong digital presence gives it a competitive edge against larger chains that charge higher margins. Its licensing partnerships also allow it to bring exclusive, high‑profile brands into the UK market, potentially boosting sales volumes.
company_30s.current_state: The company has recently survived a rough earnings season that highlighted weak FY26 numbers, but it is now pivoting toward a more profitable FY27 outlook. Management has announced a new licensing deal with Debenhams Group, and the board has secured a block listing to raise capital. The stock is currently trading at a steep discount to what analysts consider its intrinsic value, suggesting the market is still under‑appreciating its upside potential.

rns_narrative: Revolution Beauty’s latest filing shows a mixed picture: FY26 results were below expectations, but the company’s FY27 guidance looks more promising as it plans to expand its licensing portfolio and strengthen its digital sales. The AGM and block listing filings indicate that the board is actively raising capital and improving governance, which could restore investor confidence.

The company’s partnership with Debenhams Group signals a new revenue stream and a way to reach a broader customer base. Meanwhile, the block listing and voting rights updates suggest the company is consolidating shareholder support and preparing for potential strategic moves such as a sale or partnership.

Overall, the narrative is one of a company that has weathered a bad earnings season, is now focusing on growth through new licensing and digital expansion, and is taking steps to shore up its balance sheet and governance.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet optimism amid a storm of uncertainty
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls are pointing to the Debenhams deal and the board’s strong governance moves as evidence that the company is on a turnaround path. They argue that a successful licensing launch could lift sales and bring the stock back toward its intrinsic value.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears highlight the weak FY26 results, the need for significant capital infusion, and the risk that the new partnership may not generate the expected revenue. They worry that the company could still be in a deep slump if the market remains skeptical.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The chatter has stayed largely static, with no new wave of excitement. The repeated bullish posts from a single user suggest a small, echo‑chamber community rather than broad market enthusiasm.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for REVB is flat and dead, which means the market has largely ignored the stock. This creates a perfect surprise window if a catalyst emerges.

near_term_catalysts: The next quarterly earnings report could provide a clear direction if the company beats guidance or lifts its FY27 forecast.
A formal announcement of the Debenhams licensing launch, including projected revenue and sales targets, would be a strong positive signal.
Any unexpected capital raise or strategic partnership disclosed in the block listing filings could signal confidence from institutional investors.
A sudden spike in trading volume near the 4‑4.5p support zone would suggest that smart money is stepping in.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a 3‑week moving‑average crossover that confirms the stock is moving above a key support level, a jump in average daily volume to at least 30% above the 20‑day average, and any positive revision to FY27 earnings in the next RNS. Also monitor the AGM outcome for any major governance changes that could boost credibility.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early phase of a deep crash: the price has fallen well below its recent highs and the volume has dried out, indicating capitulation is near complete. A mean‑reversion move would likely need a catalyst to trigger the bounce, so patience is key until one of the above events materializes.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If the stock recovers to halfway between its 52‑week low and the last peak, the upside is roughly 200‑300% over the next 12‑18 months. The deep crash has already captured a large portion of the downside, so the remaining upside is asymmetric and attractive. The recent licensing deal and stronger governance suggest that the company is positioned to reverse its trend once the market takes notice.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The main risk is that the company may fail to deliver on its licensing promise or that the FY27 guidance remains weak. If the stock continues to trade below 4p for another six months, the downside could erode any remaining upside. A lack of capital or a failure to secure institutional support could also keep the price stuck in a low range.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss is limited to the current market cap, but the upside could more than double that if the price climbs back to 8p or higher. The risk/reward ratio is therefore heavily in favor of the upside, especially given the depth of the crash and the absence of clear terminal risks.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter around the 4‑4.5p support zone once volume spikes to at least 25% above the 20‑day average. Allocate 10–15% of your swing‑trading capital to this position, set a stop at 3.5p to protect against a brief dip, and target 8p for a 100% return. Use a trailing stop at 6p if the price starts to climb steadily.
playbook.if_watching: Hold off until the next earnings release or a formal licensing announcement. If the stock trades above 4p for 3 consecutive days with volume 20% higher than average, consider a small entry to test the new support level.
playbook.if_passing: There are no imminent delisting or bankruptcy risks, so the setup remains bullish. If the company were to announce a hostile takeover or a forced liquidation, that would trigger a sell‑off.

ai_insights.bottom_line: Revolution Beauty is sitting on a deep crash that could rebound sharply once its new licensing partnership and improved governance signal a turnaround, offering a highly asymmetric upside if the market finally recognizes its value.
